answer.message: You owe $12 in excise tax on 4 bottles of wine (13% ABV). This is your first exemption in 30 days, so you must declare and pay the tax.
You owe $10 in excise tax on the vodka. No duty is due. Declare the vodka at customs.
You owe $14.00 in duty for 3 bottles of South African Pinotage. This is the total amount due for your return.
You owe $13.50 in excise tax on the rum. No duty is due. Declare the bottles at customs upon arrival.
You owe $2.50 in excise tax on the Canadian whisky. No duty is due. Declare it upon return to the U.S.
You owe $1.00 in excise tax on the two 50 ml rum miniatures. This is the only duty owed. Declare them upon return to the U.S.
You owe $20.00 for the second carton of British cigarettes. This includes $10.00 duty and $10.00 excise tax. Declare the cigarettes upon arrival.
Cuban cigars are prohibited from importation into the United States. You cannot bring them into the country.
As a U.S. resident returning from abroad, you may bring 1 liter of wine (up to 1.5 liters if you're 21+). You owe $1.00 in excise tax on the wine. Duty is waived.
You owe $2.00 in duties and excise taxes for the tequila and cigarettes. Declare them upon return to the U.S.
You owe $20.00 in duties and excise taxes for 2 bottles of Scotch and 5 packs of cigarettes. Declare them at customs upon arrival.
As a US resident returning from Italy, you may bring back 1 liter of alcohol (1 bottle of 750 ml) duty-free. Since the value is under $5, no duty or excise tax is owed.
You owe $1.80 in duty for 2 bottles of Portuguese red wine. This is the standard rate for alcohol under 14% ABV.
You owe $12 in excise tax on the 2 bottles of gin. No duty is due. Declare the alcohol upon arrival.
You owe $1.50 in excise tax on the 3 bottles of wine. No duty is owed. Declare the wine upon arrival.
Nicotine pouches are not covered by this tool. For customs rules on nicotine products, consult the U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) website or contact a customs officer directly.
As a flight attendant, you are not a returning US resident and are subject to different customs rules. Please consult a customs officer for details.
You cannot 'hide' items from customs. All items must be declared. Attempting to evade customs is illegal and may result in penalties.
